reason: ESET update proxy deliberately denies signed update resources and removes update-routing sections, with self-image hash rotation, competing-listener termination and HKLM Run persistence.
method: Static UPX decompression, cleave facts, Rizin disassembly/control-flow inspection, and non-executed byte-mutation controls. Neither sample nor endpoints were executed/contacted.

functions.behavior: Handles standby mutation, direct mutation, autostart and no-rotation flags. Relocates to its expected basename, obtains a single-instance mutex, performs rotation handoff, registers autostart, starts the proxy thread and runs a hidden window/message loop.
Opens the specified image for read/write with up to 25 retries and 100 ms sleeps, seeds rand using timing and process ID, seeks to EOF, and appends 4 through 11 random bytes.

Creates a temporary eup_rotate_<pid>.exe copy with CREATE_NO_WINDOW. The standby waits up to 60 seconds for the original process, sleeps 700 ms, mutates the original image, and relaunches it with -no-rotate.
Writes its quoted full path as an HKLM CurrentVersion Run value. If elevated access is needed, requests ShellExecuteW runas with -autostart. No UAC bypass was established.

Binds TCP 8000 on INADDR_ANY. On bind failure, resolves GetExtendedTcpTable, searches for the listener owner, excludes PID <=4 and itself, and attempts TerminateProcess after checking STILL_ACTIVE. Accepts clients into the update-proxy handler.

Parses HTTP request targets. A suffix comparison against .signed reaches a 404 Not Found response at 0x414e8a..0x414e96. Rewrites update.ver paths and forwards requests to a fixed ESET upstream using a remotely selected account. This is not evidence of an open proxy, remote shell or arbitrary C2 task dispatch.
Recognizes [SERVERS], [LINKS] and [HOSTS], sets per-section skip flags, and discards their headings and contents until another INI heading. Other lines are appended to the forwarded response.

Decodes four strings with output[i] = input[i] XOR key XOR ((31*i+7)&255), assembles https://id.1yz.me:4046/id.html, and fetches an account list with embedded Basic credentials. Strips HTML, parses account candidates, tests them against an ESET update manifest and caches a working pair. No local credential-store collection was found.

On a secure-request error, passes option 31 and flags 0x3300 to the dynamically resolved WinHttpSetOption pointer and retries. Unlike the previously reviewed 4.0.1 specimens, this build really relaxes certificate checks; the existing suspicious trait correctly matches.

Fetches HTTP info.txt, parses version/downurl, and asks through MessageBoxW. Only IDYES (6) reaches executable replacement. Checks downloaded bytes for MZ, swaps the current image to .old.exe, launches the replacement and opens an explanatory page. No cryptographic verification was found. User approval prevents classifying this path alone as silent payload execution.
USER32 timers trigger ESET ecmd.exe /update, check program updates every 600000 ms and rotate the executable every 21600000 ms. The cron diagnostic is not OS cron or Task Scheduler persistence.

coverage.trait_changes: None needed: existing traits cover the confirmed behavior without relying on the collector filename or exact endpoint.

validation.controls: Positive; renamed product/IP; changed affine decoder constants and concealed host; removed signed-resource predicate; unreferenced suffix; non-404 response; unreferenced section heading; no rotation diagnostic; no autostart success; no termination API; protocol option instead of trust relaxation; standard HTTPS port.

limitations: Static analysis does not establish runtime success, endpoint ownership, or the precise ESET client's signature-fallback behavior.
Future self-update payloads and live account-list contents were not retrieved.
The hostile findings share independently confirmed update-tampering context; ordinary networking, registry writes, product identity and UPX alone are not convictions.
